## Overview
### Introduction to Google: Nano Banana 2
The Google: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview) is a cutting-edge language model developed by Google, released on January 1, 2024. As a standard-tier model, it is not open-source. This model is part of the Gemini series and is designed to provide high-quality text generation and analysis capabilities. With its robust architecture, it can handle a wide range of tasks, including chat, text generation, coding, analysis, and summarization.

### Technical Specifications and Strengths
The Google: Nano Banana 2 model boasts an impressive context window of 65,536 tokens and a maximum output of 65,536 tokens. Its pricing structure is as follows: $0.5 per 1M tokens for input, $3.0 per 1M tokens for output, with no charges for cached input or batch input. The model's capabilities include text, function calling, JSON mode, streaming, and structured outputs. Its strengths are reflected in its benchmark scores, including an MMLU score of 80.0 and an LMSYS Arena ELO score of 1200. The model is best suited for applications such as chat, text generation, coding, analysis, and summarization.

### Use Cases and Cost Considerations
Developers can leverage the Google: Nano Banana 2 model for a variety of use cases, including building conversational AI systems, generating high-quality text, and performing complex analysis tasks. When considering the cost of using this model, developers can expect to pay $0.0018 for 1,000 calls with an average of 500 tokens, $0.018 for 10,000 calls, and $0.18 for 100,000 calls. With its unique set of capabilities and competitive pricing, the Google: Nano Banana 2 model is an attractive option for developers looking to integrate advanced language processing capabilities into their applications. The Google: Nano Banana 2 model excels in chat and text generation tasks due to its high context window of 65,536 tokens. This makes it ideal for generating coherent and contextually relevant text.

```

# Generate code based on a specification

print(response)
```
